# Type Coverage Ratchet

Status: real gate with a temporary ratchet.

`pnpm check:types-coverage` runs:

```bash
type-coverage --project tsconfig.type-coverage.json --at-least 99.7
```

The current gate is a source-only metric over real production and tooling files
selected by `tsconfig.type-coverage.json`. Co-located `*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`,
`__tests__`, and dedicated test trees are excluded from this percentage because
fixture-heavy test expressions would dilute the production-code signal. Tests
remain covered by the repo's strict TypeScript typechecks; this split changes
metric ownership, not compiler enforcement.

Literal Starter and Registry source with a hash-verified `adapted: false`
receipt is measured as immutable vendored authority rather than locally authored
code. The gate derives exact file arguments from both receipts; any
`adapted: true` entry keeps that destination measured across both receipts.

## Ratchet Rule

- Never lower the threshold.
- Raise the threshold when a cleanup pass removes uncovered positions.
- The target is 100%.
- Do not exclude production source files to improve the number. The only paid
  source exception is an exact hash-verified, unadapted receipt destination.
- Keep conventional test files and test-only trees outside this source metric;
  enforce them with strict TypeScript instead.
- Generated files may be excluded only when they are regenerated by Confect,
  Convex, or other checked generators.

## Cleanup Focus

Prioritize uncovered production and tooling source until the ratchet reaches
100%. Test typing improvements belong to the strict TypeScript gates.
